prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your location in Atlanta, budget, the size/age of your home, whether you want a high-efficiency system or a budget replacement, and how important things like warranties, financing, or same‑day install are to you.

I can find and compare top local companies for you, but first a few quick questions so I can give a targeted recommendation:
- What is your ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta?
- Is this a residential or commercial system?
- Roughly how many square feet is the home and how many HVAC zones/air handlers?
- Do you prefer a specific brand (Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Goodman, Rheem, etc.)?
- Do you have a target budget or need financing?
- How soon do you need the replacement?

If you want to act now, here are objective steps and a checklist to find the best local installer and avoid common pitfalls:

What to look for in an installer
- Proper licensing and insurance for Georgia contractors.
- NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer certifications (for the brand you choose).
- Good, recent online reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi and a solid BBB rating.
- Local references and examples of similar installs.
- Willingness to perform a Manual J load calculation (correct sizing) and a duct evaluation.
- Clear written estimate with equipment model numbers, SEER rating, price breakdown (equipment vs. labor), tax, permit and disposal fees, start/finish dates.
- Clear warranty details (manufacturer vs. labor), and any extended labor warranties available.
- Agreement to pull permits and follow local code.

Questions to ask when getting quotes
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation for sizing?
- What is included in the installation (new pad, line set, thermostat, refrigerant charge, ductwork repairs)?
- Will you test and balance the airflow? Do you perform a combustion safety test (if applicable)?
- Who will be my point of contact? Do you subcontract or use your own technicians?
- What are your payment options and do you offer financing?
- How long is the job estimated to take?

Typical cost and equipment notes (Atlanta, rough ranges)
- Small/straightforward replacement (single‑story, existing ductwork, basic 13–14 SEER): ~$3,500–$6,000.
- Mid‑range (higher SEER 16–18, minor ductwork or complexity): ~$6,000–$9,500.
- High‑end installs (top-tier brands, major ductwork, heat pump options, larger homes): $9,500–$15,000+.
(Actual price depends on tonnage, SEER, ductwork, access and local labor.)

Brands & approach
- Brand matters less than proper sizing and quality of installation. Trane, Carrier, Lennox often cost more but have strong reputations; Goodman and Amana are budget-friendly. Rheem/Ruud are solid mid-range choices.
- Consider a heat pump if you want both cooling and efficient heating (especially with Atlanta’s milder winters).

If you want, I can:
- Pull the top-rated HVAC installers in your ZIP with links to reviews and comments on strengths/weaknesses.
- Prepare a shortlist of 3–5 companies to call and a script of questions to use on each.
Tell me your ZIP code and priorities and I’ll find the best local options.
